questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Cosine Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x+{50}^{∘})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=-{1}^{∘}+n\cdot {72}^{∘},\,x={b}^{∘}+n\cdot {72}^{∘},
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $b?$
questions.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+{50}^{∘} & ={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & 5x+{50}^{∘} & ={315}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & =-{5}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & 5x & ={265}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ x & =-{1}^{∘}+n\cdot {72}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={53}^{∘}+n\cdot {72}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $b=53.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Reciprocal Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric  equation:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3}-\frac{\pi }{12})=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a+6\pi n,\,x=-\frac{3\pi }{4}+6\pi n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{3}-\frac{\pi }{12})=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\frac{x}{3}-\frac{\pi }{12}=-\frac{2\pi }{3}+2n\pi ,\,\frac{x}{3}-\frac{\pi }{12}=-\frac{\pi }{3}+2\pi n.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{3}=\frac{\pi }{12}-\frac{2\pi }{3}+2n\pi , & \,\frac{x}{3}=\frac{\pi }{12}-\frac{2\pi }{3}+2n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{3}=-\frac{7\pi }{12}+2n\pi , & \,\frac{x}{3}=-\frac{\pi }{4}+2n\pi  \\ x=-\frac{7\pi }{4}+6n\pi , & \,x=-\frac{3\pi }{4}+6n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have that $a=-\frac{7\pi }{4}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x={a}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},
$$

 

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
questions.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & ={30}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2\cdot {30}^{∘}+2\cdot n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a={60}^{∘}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡(3x)=-\sqrt{3}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a\pi +\frac{n\pi }{3},
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
questions.worked_solution:
The given equation is equivalent to 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡3x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.
$$

So, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{\pi }{18}+\frac{n\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a=-\frac{1}{18}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Reciprocal Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric  equation:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x={180}^{∘}+n\cdot 1\,{080}^{∘},\,x={a}^{∘}+n\cdot 1\,{080}^{∘},
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\frac{x}{3}={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},\,\frac{x}{3}={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
x={180}^{∘}+n\cdot 1\,{080}^{∘},\,x={360}^{∘}+n\cdot 1\,{080}^{∘}\,\,
$$

So, we have that $a=360.$
